out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: in the walk- in refrigerator, raw chicken was being stored over cooked chicken. Also in the walk-in refrigerator, raw shell eggs were being stored over fully cooked and ready to eat samosas. In the 1DR UPR Pepsi cooler behind cash had raw shell eggs being stored over cans of soda.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL RAW FOODS NEED TO BE STORED BELOW READY TO EAT FOODS TO PREVENT POTENTIAL CONTAMINATION. PIC MOVED ALL RAW FOODS IN BOTH COOLERS TO BELOW THE READY TO EAT FOODS.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Cooked samosas in the 2DR UPR sliding door cooler in BOH were temping at 51F at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COLD HOLDING FOODS SHOULD TEMP AT 41F OR BELOW. PIC THREW AWAY THE SAMOSAS THAT WERE TEMPING AT 51F.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: whole cucumber was moldy and soft to the touch. It had been stored in the walk-in refrigerator for longer than 7 days.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. PIC THREW AWAY MOLDY CUCUMBER.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: Multiple food items in the walk-in refrigerator did not have a date mark on them.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS PROVIDED GUIDANCE ON HOW FOOD ITEMS STORED FOR LONGER THAN 24 HOURS NEED A DATE MARKING ON THEM. PIC WILL OBTAIN STICKERS AND BEGIN LABELING ALL FOOD ITEMS KEPT LONGER THAN 24 HOURS. PIC WILL SEND EHS A PICTURE OF THE DATE MARKED ITEMS IN 10 DAYS.

violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wash their hands and exposed portions of their arms by: 1) discarding used gloves; 2) rinsing under warm running water; 3) applying soap; 4) rubbing together for at least 10-15 seconds; 5) rinsing thoroughly under warm running water; and 6) drying with paper towels or air drying device. CDI Ehs instructed to use soap

violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. CDI Ehs instructed employee to discard food and wash hands. Employee hid the fruit in the refrigerator and did not use soap when washing hands. EHS instructed to use soap and discard the food.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: food left on the floor/counter in deep plastic containers for over 6hours.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI discussed cooling again. Provided cooling hand out again.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name

violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. and must be stored in reusable containers
